name: Offer ancillary services
summary: The AESO buys operating reserves (regulating, spinning and supplemental, active and standby) a day ahead in short open auctions on the Watt-Ex platform each weekday morning, and the company's hydro units, battery and converted gas units are among the main sellers. Portfolio analysts list the reserve-capable MW and estimate the energy margin given up, the real-time trader offers MW and a premium or discount to pool price for each product and block, watches the open book until each auction closes, designates delivering assets and reshapes the energy offers before the noon energy deadline. The session is short but tightly timed, and an award that is not reflected in the energy offers or not planned in the plants turns into a delivery failure later.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator whose reservoir hydro, 10 MW battery and converted gas units sell operating reserves through a 24-hour real-time desk.
baseline.notes: Watt-Ex day-ahead auctions from 9:00 on weekdays with sequential closes, as described by the MSA (2009) and CRA (2023); ISO rule 205.1 (2014 rule, 2023 drafting update).

unit_of_work: one Watt-Ex trading session of reserve offers (one or more delivery days)
trigger: The AESO posts its reserve requirements and bid prices for the next delivery day or days on Watt-Ex ahead of the 9:00 weekday session.
end_state: Reserve offers have cleared or lapsed, delivering assets are designated, next-day energy offers exclude the reserved MW, plants have the reserve schedule and the awards are booked.

volume.seasonality: One session per business day; Friday and pre-holiday sessions buy two to four delivery days.

evidence.note: Trading windows run each weekday (CRA 2023) and 205.1 has a separate deadline for multi-day procurement, so sessions equal business days. The organisation file shows 28 to 31 cases (one per calendar day).
About 2.5 to 3 hours of trader time per session.
About 1.5 hours of analysis per session, more on Fridays.
Daily approval; not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Water-limit checks and reserve planning; not listed for this process in the organisation file.
Battery state-of-charge plans; not listed for this process in the organisation file.

systems.name: AESO Energy Trading System (offers, declarations and dispatch)
Energy trading and risk management system
Load, price, wind and inflow forecasting models
Hydro, wind and battery SCADA and remote control
Document management and engineering drawings repository
Recorded desk and control room phone lines

resources.name: Hydro plant with dam and reservoir

steps.name: AESO posts reserve requirements
steps.description: Before the trading session the AESO posts on the Watt-Ex platform the MW it wants to buy for the next day (or for several days before a weekend or holiday) for each reserve product and period, with its bid price that caps active offers.

evidence.note: AESO announces a required volume and a bid price at the start of each auction (CRA 2023).

steps.name: List reserve-capable MW by asset
steps.description: The portfolio optimisation analyst lists, for each hydro unit, the battery and each converted gas unit, the MW it is qualified and able to provide as regulating, spinning or supplemental reserve tomorrow, after outages, derates and planned energy output.

error.defect_description: An asset out for maintenance is listed as able to carry reserve.

next.condition: Friday or pre-holiday session buying several days

evidence.note: Qualified quantities and multi-day procurement in 205.1 s.2(3) and s.3(3); reserve products from MSA 2009. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Extend the plan over the weekend
steps.description: For a session that buys reserves for Saturday to Monday or a holiday, the analyst extends the capability list and price view to each extra delivery day, using the weekend wind and load forecast and the weekend water schedule.

error.defect_description: Weekend outage missed for one day.

evidence.note: Weekday-only trading windows (CRA 2023) and the 13:00 multi-day designation deadline (205.1 s.2(3)(b)) imply multi-day sessions; times are estimates.

steps.name: Confirm water limits for holding reserve
steps.description: The hydro control centre operator confirms reservoir and forebay levels, minimum and maximum flows and any ice limits that decide whether hydro units can sit part-loaded with headroom for reserve through the on-peak and off-peak blocks.

evidence.note: Hydro is the main reserve provider for the company (organisation file, src3 there); the check is an estimate.

steps.name: Estimate the opportunity cost of reserves
steps.description: The analyst forecasts the on-peak and off-peak pool price and its volatility, works out the energy margin given up for each MW held as reserve, and compares it with recent equilibrium prices to suggest a premium or discount to pool price for each product.

error.defect_description: Volatility underestimated, so reserves are sold below the energy margin given up.

evidence.note: Participants estimate pool price and foregone energy profits before each auction (CRA 2023 quoting LEI); times are estimates.

steps.name: Choose reserve volumes and prices
steps.description: The real-time trader decides how many MW of each asset to offer in each product and block, active or standby, and the index (premium or discount to pool price) for each offer, balancing reserve revenue against keeping water and capacity for the energy market.

error.defect_description: Same MW planned for energy and reserve.

evidence.note: Offer content from 205.1 s.3; indexing to pool price from CRA 2023. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Lead approves the reserve plan
steps.description: The real-time desk lead reviews the planned MW and indices against the energy strategy for the day and the water position, approves them or asks for changes before the 9:00 window opens.

control.basis: Trading authority and risk policy: desk lead approval of daily reserve strategy

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Enter active regulating reserve offers
steps.description: When the Watt-Ex window opens at 9:00 the trader enters the active regulating reserve offers for each block, MW and index, which close first, at about 9:40.

error.defect_description: MW entered for the wrong block.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 205.1 s.2 and s.3: offers through the AESO-specified trading platform, per on-peak, off-peak and super-peak period, same MW each hour, at least 5 MW, active price not above the AESO bid price

evidence.note: 9:00 opening and close times from MSA 2009 and CRA 2023; entry time is an estimate.

steps.name: Enter spinning and supplemental offers
steps.description: The trader enters the active spinning reserve offers (closing about 9:50) and supplemental reserve offers (closing about 10:00) for the hydro units, battery and gas units that can provide them.

error.defect_description: Offer for an asset not qualified for the product.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 205.1 s.2 and s.3: offers through the AESO-specified trading platform, per on-peak, off-peak and super-peak period, same MW each hour, at least 5 MW, active price not above the AESO bid price

evidence.note: Sequential closes ten minutes apart; entry times are estimates.

steps.name: Watch the open book and adjust
steps.description: Because Watt-Ex shows all offers as they are entered, the trader watches the stack form for each product and revises indices or MW before each close, within the limits the lead approved.

evidence.note: Open auction with offers visible in real time (CRA 2023); time is an estimate.

steps.name: Auctions close and clear
steps.description: Each active auction closes in turn and the AESO accepts offers in merit order up to its requirement; Watt-Ex shows the cleared MW for each offer and the equilibrium price, the average of the AESO bid price and the clearing offer.

evidence.note: Acceptance in merit order (205.1 s.5) and equilibrium pricing (CRA 2023); shares are estimates.

steps.name: Enter standby reserve offers
steps.description: The trader enters standby offers, each with a premium of at most 99 CAD/MWh for being available and an activation price for being called, for capacity not sold in the active auctions, before the standby closes at about 10:10 to 10:30.

error.defect_description: Activation price below the energy value of the capacity.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 205.1 s.3(2)(b): standby premium up to 99 CAD/MWh and activation price

evidence.note: Standby price structure (205.1) and close times (MSA 2009); time is an estimate.

steps.name: Standby auctions clear
steps.description: The standby auctions close and Watt-Ex shows the standby MW accepted for each asset with the premium and activation price, which the desk adds to the day's reserve position.

evidence.note: Standby closes 10:10 to 10:30; estimate of time to see results.

steps.name: Designate assets for the awards
steps.description: Where offers were made from a pooled virtual asset, the trader designates which pool assets will deliver each awarded MW, by 11:30 for a one-day session or 13:00 for a multi-day session, and checks every award maps to a qualified asset.

error.defect_description: Award designated to an asset that is short of headroom.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 205.1 s.2(3): designate delivering pool assets by 11:30 (one day) or 13:00 (multiple days)

evidence.note: Deadlines stated in 205.1 s.2(3); time is an estimate.

steps.name: Reshape next-day energy offers
steps.description: Before the 12:00 energy offer deadline the trader changes the next-day energy offers of the assets carrying reserve, so the MW held for reserve are not also offered as energy and the offer still reflects the unit's real capability.

error.defect_description: Reserve MW left in the energy offer, so the unit is dispatched into its own reserve.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.1 s.2(2)(a): energy offers before 12:00 on the day before delivery

evidence.note: Energy deadline (203.1) and concurrent energy and reserve rules (203.4 s.7); the practice and time are estimates.

steps.name: Send the reserve schedule to the plants
steps.description: The trader emails and calls the hydro control centre, the gas control rooms and the operations centre with the reserve schedule: which asset carries which product, in which hours, and how many MW of headroom to keep.

error.defect_description: Schedule sent with the wrong hours.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Plan hydro units to hold reserve
steps.description: The hydro control centre operator plans which units will run part-loaded or stay synchronised to carry the awarded regulating and spinning reserve, and how that fits the day's water release, then holds the plants to that plan through the delivery day.

error.defect_description: Plan leaves too little headroom in one hour.

evidence.note: Estimate; on-peak block is 07:00 to 23:00 (16 hours) per CRA 2023, which sets the plant occupancy mode.

steps.name: Plan the battery state of charge
steps.description: The renewables operations centre operator sets the battery's state-of-charge plan so it can follow regulating signals or deliver contingency reserve through the awarded hours without running empty or full.

evidence.note: Estimate; the battery entered service in 2020 (organisation file).

steps.name: Book the awards
steps.description: The trader enters the cleared reserve MW, prices and designations in the ETRM so settlement analysts can check the AESO statement and the profit and loss shows reserve revenue, and files the session record.

error.defect_description: Award booked at the wrong index.

control.basis: Trade capture for settlement reconciliation and risk reporting

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Multi-day session
exceptions.description: Friday or pre-holiday session buys reserves for two to four delivery days, so the capability list and price view are extended and designations are due by 13:00.

exceptions.name: Lead asks for changes
exceptions.description: The desk lead changes reserve volumes or indices before the window opens.

exceptions.name: Nothing cleared
exceptions.description: All offers were priced out of merit, so no reserve is carried and the energy offers stand as prepared.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the start of preparation (about 07:00) to booked awards
benchmarks.population: Daily operating reserve sessions of an Alberta generator, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Derived from the 9:00 window, closes between 9:40 and 10:30 and designation by 11:30 or 13:00; the start time of preparation is an estimate.
2009 schedule; CRA 2023 confirms the same sequence ten minutes apart from a 9:00 window.

pain_points.description: The reserve auctions close at about 10:00 and the energy offers are due at 12:00, so awards must be turned into reshaped energy offers and designations within two hours, with the risk that reserve MW are left in the energy offer.

evidence.note: Deadlines from the rules; the error risk is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Reserve offers are priced as a premium or discount to a pool price nobody knows yet, so the trader must judge the energy margin given up on volatile days.
Plants learn their reserve duty from an email and a phone call, and a missed headroom plan becomes a reserve delivery failure, the costliest ISO rule penalty area in 2021.

evidence.note: Sections 205.6 and 205.5 carried the highest specified penalty totals in 2021 (74,000 and 21,250 CAD).

sources.title: ISO Rules Section 203.1, Offers and Bids for Energy (effective 2013-12-20)
sources.supports: Offers due before 12:00 on the day before the delivery day and no earlier than 7 days before; offer for every settlement interval for source assets of 5 MW or more; prices of at least 0 and under 1,000 CAD/MWh; block MW, flexible or inflexible flag and minimum stable generation; top block equals maximum capability; available capability equal to maximum capability unless an acceptable operational reason is given; ramp rate and initial start-up time; standing submissions; ETS acknowledgement and valid or invalid notice.

sources.title: ISO Rules Section 203.4, Delivery Requirements for Energy (2023-03-31 administrative version; substantive text from 2020-09-16)
sources.supports: Respond to dispatches with reasonable dispatch protocols, personnel and software; start moving toward the dispatched MW within 10 minutes of the dispatch time; reach steady state within the ramp time plus 40 percent (at least 5 minutes) plus 10 minutes; stay inside the allowable dispatch variance over 10-minute periods; restate within 20 minutes if an operational deviation lasts 20 minutes or longer. The revision history shows the 2023 version only aligned drafting with the 2020 text.

sources.title: ISO Rules Section 205.1, Offers for Operating Reserve (2023-03-31 drafting update of the 2014-12-23 rule)
sources.supports: Operating reserve offers through the electronic trading platform the AESO specifies; offers per on-peak, off-peak and super-peak period with the same MW in each hour and at least 5 MW; active offers as a premium or discount to pool price not above the AESO bid price; standby offers with a premium (max 99 CAD/MWh) and activation price; designation of pool assets for virtual-asset awards by 11:30 (one day) or 13:00 (multiple days); over-the-counter fallback; AESO accepts offers in merit order at the close of trading.

sources.title: Assessment of AESO Recommendations to Adopt a Sealed-Bid Auction for Operating Reserves (A. Baziliauskas and A. Yatchew, Charles River Associates)
sources.supports: Operating reserves bought day-ahead by the AESO as sole buyer on the Watt-Ex exchange; auctions close in sequence ten minutes apart (active regulating, spinning, supplemental, then standby products); time blocks on-peak 07:00-23:00, off-peak, AM and PM super-peak; offers during an hour-long window starting at 9:00 each weekday; open book where offers are visible as entered; equilibrium price is the average of the AESO bid price and the clearing offer, added to pool price; participants estimate pool price and foregone energy margin before offering; TransAlta and other large participants commented in the 2022 review.

sources.title: Operating Reserves Procurement: Understanding Market Outcomes (2009-09-16)
sources.supports: Watt-Ex day-ahead trading from 9:00 with closes at 9:40 (active regulating), 9:50 (spinning), 10:00 (supplemental), 10:10 to 10:30 (standby products), with over-the-counter trades after close; typical procured volumes (about 110 to 165 MW regulating, 170 to 260 MW spinning and supplemental); standby suppliers have fifteen minutes to get into position.

sources.title: MSA Compliance Review 2021 (April 5, 2022)
sources.supports: 462 ISO rules matters addressed in 2021 (437 in 2020), 91 percent self-reported; 75 notices of specified penalty totalling 129,250 CAD; 114 matters under section 203.3 (restatements), 83 under 203.4 (dispatch delivery), 67 under 201.7 (dispatch acknowledgement), 43 under 205.6 and 26 under 205.5 (reserves); 74 percent of matters closed with forbearance; TransAlta entities among those penalised.

assumptions: One case is one Watt-Ex trading session, not one calendar day. Sessions run on business days, so the volume is about 21 a month rather than the organisation file's 28 to 31.

Watt-Ex timing (window from 9:00, closes from 9:40 to 10:30) is taken from the MSA's 2009 description and the 2023 CRA assessment, which describe the same design; it is assumed unchanged in 2019-2022.

Step resources show capacity held for reserve: a hydro plant for 8 to 24 hours and the battery for 4 to 16 hours per session. Only part of the plant's MW is held, but the plant cannot be scheduled freely in those hours.
Over-the-counter reserve trades after the auctions (allowed under 205.1 s.4 and noted by the MSA in 2009) are not modelled.
Partner-operated unit shares are not offered as reserve by this desk.

Times are estimates; the AESO and MSA documents give deadlines, not durations. The simulated median runs longer than the 0.25-day benchmark because the simulation adds every hands-on minute and wait in sequence, while in practice the analyst and trader prepare in parallel before 9:00 and the open-book watching overlaps the offer entry.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
